title: Derivative chromosome 22 — t(9;22)
clinical_history: Identify pter, p, centromere, q, and qter on der(22), then construct it from chromosome 22 segments retained through 22q11.2 plus distal 9q. This models the Philadelphia chromosome. Demonstration map only.
hints: der(22) keeps 22pter through 22q11.2 and then continues with 9q34→9qter.
Material from chromosome 9 on a 22-derived centromere is a derivative, not a second intact chromosome 9.
The balanced karyotype is written t(9;22)(q34;q11.2); the small der(22) is the Philadelphia chromosome.
anatomy_hints: The centromere matches chromosome 22. Distal long-arm bands do not.
Name the rearrangement class and the two chromosomes whose q-arm bands meet on this map.
explanation: The derivative is assembled by truncating the chromosome 22 map after 22q11.2 and appending distal 9q segments from the chromosome 9 map. That is the educational model of der(22)t(9;22)(q34;q11.2).
